There is definitely a volumetric difference in depth through listening with Tidal in comparison to other music apps. However, the settings are very finite, lacking an equaliser and other sound adjustments. There is also no sign-up/in with Google button which would have been nice, there are also certain functionality issues. Tidal does however have two widgets allowing easy access to the app and very basic player controls. Quality: The quality of the music is superb, crisp and punchy even on Stereo. Whilst my device doesn't support Dolby Atmos, I have no doubt in my mind that the music quality would sound even better with it. Tidal also offers choices of streaming and download quality ranging from 'normal' to Hi-Fi or Master Quality. Pricing: Tidal can perhaps the most expensive of its competitors, however, for those with an itch for the purest of audio, it's definitely worth a look at and Tidal have trial options that do not take payment details which can be very enticing. Privacy: I am seeing a lot of DNS entries to advertisers and data brokers on both the Mobile and Desktop app which I was not happy with as I was unable to use either until I had allowed each entry through despite those ones tracking across the web, I also struggled to sign on using a VPN, returning errors. However, otherwise seems to work fine past the sign-in stage. What I would like to see before I commit to Tidal. More settings including an in-app equaliser. Cut down on the tracking and make the tracking less integrated so that users with firewalls or VPNs can load the app and browse your website properly, even with tracking blocked. Whilst I do understand from a security perspective regarding data collection, users should not have to compromise on privacy, especially for a music app. Lasstly, I'd like to see more controls on the music widgets and in app, specifically jumping to previous songs and some sort of dislike button (maybe a broken heart (keeping with the theme)).
